solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Preserve prepared ideas for reform

parts.note: something prepared or ready is set, as in 'all set'

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their freshly worked-out ideas in reserve until a reform programme comes along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' reads as describing the ideas, but it is the synonym for the first word; 'for reform' rearranges the ideas to give ASIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something back for later use is to reserve or preserve it.

clue.text: Slipshod line over work admitted by agent

indicators.note: the pieces are let into, or admitted by, the other word

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A careless secret agent lets slip work done on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod and sloppy are both synonyms for careless and untidy.

clue.text: Liquid put into GT — problem for a driver?

indicators.note: liquid means fluid or not fixed, so the letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: Fuel poured into a sports car, a worry for whoever drives it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid' looks like the fuel but signals the anagram. In UK law, totting up is the adding of penalty points on a licence, leading to a ban at twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Under UK licensing rules, accumulating penalty points can cost a motorist their licence, a real problem for drivers.

clue.text: Situation patron manufactured putting limit on possible number

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up, so the letters are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A patron creates a situation by capping the number allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: The point at which no more can be absorbed or accepted is a limit on how many is possible.

clue.text: A European expedition held up relating to some trawling?

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding the pieces up means reading them from bottom to top

parts.note: expedition can mean speed or promptness

explanation.surface: A European expedition is delayed; it concerns some fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' reverses A E SPEED in this down clue, and 'expedition' means haste, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Some trawling is done far out on the ocean, so deep-sea fishing describes it.

clue.text: Worthless cap fool returned

indicators.note: something returned is sent back, so the two words are read backwards

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle
a nit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A cheap hat sent back by a silly buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot is an informal adjective for something shoddy, petty or of little value.

clue.text: Arranged timeline by a trip — such creates difficulty in understanding?

indicators.note: letters arranged afresh are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A trip's timeline is so muddled it is hard to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Impenetrability describes text or ideas so obscure they resist comprehension.

clue.text: Attractive figure revealing speed?

definitions.meaning: a glamorous person whose poster is stuck on a wall
a speedometer's needle or pin rising shows how fast you are going

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer: a pin (needle) going up reveals speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is an attractive person in a poster; a needle rising on a dial shows speed.

clue.text: Stream in article on Republican makes for exciting story

indicators.note: the stream goes in, inside the article

parts.note: 'the' is the definite article
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a Republican and a stream makes gripping reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is a suspenseful novel or film, an exciting story.

clue.text: Guy attracts heart of girls? Tricky question

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A man draws the affection of girls; a puzzling matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is the verb to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a puzzling problem, a brain-teaser.

clue.text: Group that plays in part of autumn blockbuster

parts.note: October, abbreviated Oct, is an autumn month
E.T. was Spielberg's hugely successful 1982 film

explanation.surface: A band performs in a big film released in the autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble of eight musicians is the musical group meant here.

clue.text: Speaker's first person by one leading strikers — notable revelation?

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard, so the pronoun is replaced by a word sounding the same

parts.note: the first-person singular pronoun is I
in cricket an opener is a batsman who goes in first, leading the strikers

explanation.surface: Someone describes the top person beside the leader of a strike: a striking revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker's' turns I into the same-sounding EYE. In cricket the striker is the batsman facing the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surprising that suddenly shows you the truth is an informal eye-opener.

clue.text: Sits taking in border by river and flowers

indicators.note: one word takes in, or contains, the other pieces

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so 'sits' is poses
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: Someone posing for a picture in a riverside border full of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Primroses are pale yellow spring plants, examples of flowers.

clue.text: Note for vacation taken by friend in mountainous country

indicators.note: vacating the word empties it, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A holiday note left by a friend who has gone off to the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan kingdom, home of Everest, is a famously mountainous country.

clue.text: Saga that incorporates female

indicators.note: the words incorporate, or contain, the letters needed

explanation.surface: A long story that includes a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporates' points to the letters held within 'Saga that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is a woman's name, as in Agatha Christie, so it stands for a female.

clue.text: Artist gets to detect futile competition

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for an artist
to trace something is to find or detect it

explanation.surface: A painter finds out about a pointless contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is an idiom for the endless struggle for wealth or status.

clue.text: A name located possibly regarding telling of story

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A name found, perhaps, in connection with a tale being told.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal means based on or relating to personal stories rather than facts.

clue.text: Inactivity I had seen before contact about two points

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: about means around, so the word goes around the points

parts.note: a contact is a lens worn on the eye
E and S, east and south, are two compass points

explanation.surface: Idleness: I had seen it before getting in touch about a couple of details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contact' here is a contact lens, not a person you get in touch with; 'about' wraps it round the two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is the state of doing nothing, that is lack of activity.

clue.text: Old map I mistook for official document

indicators.note: the letters are taken wrongly, that is jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confuses an old map with an official paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is a certificate awarded by a college or school, an official document.

clue.text: Business in a trade show announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the words are replaced by ones sounding the same

parts.note: a fair is a trade show, so with the article this is 'a fair'

explanation.surface: A firm's dealings are revealed at an exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair can be a matter or concern, so it means business, as in 'that's my business'.

clue.text: Engineer has met capital banker

indicators.note: to engineer something is to contrive or rework it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineer has met a banker in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is a river, something with banks; this one flows through London.
explanation.definitionFit: London's river is the capital's banker: a flowing thing with banks.

clue.text: Raise corruption virtually dominant in city

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word reads it upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to be on top is to be dominant

explanation.surface: Stirring up corruption that is almost everywhere in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' reverses ROT upward in this down clue; 'virtually' cuts ONTOP to ONTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the largest city in Canada.

clue.text: Consecutively arguing?

definitions.meaning: one after another without a break
row, rhyming with cow, is a quarrel, so having a row is arguing

explanation.definitionFit: One after another means successively; being in a quarrel means disputing.

clue.text: Supply online joke?

parts.note: e- is the prefix for electronic or online, as in email
a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: Providing a wisecrack on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to furnish or provide them with what they need.

clue.text: Customary pub so usable on a regular basis

indicators.note: letters are taken at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: A local pub is routinely made fit for use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a regular basis' takes every second letter of 'pub so usable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual and customary are synonyms for normal or habitual.

clue.text: Supporting duke beset by old vice that's taboo

parts.note: to be for something is to support it

indicators.note: the piece is surrounded, or beset, by the other

parts.note: Joe Biden was formerly US vice-president

explanation.surface: Backing an aristocrat caught up in an old vice that's off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old vice' looks like a long-standing sin but is a former vice-president.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is prohibited by custom, that is banned or not allowed.

clue.text: Regret in short cutting form of text in learning

indicators.note: the shortened word cuts into the other one

parts.note: an edition is a particular published form of a text

indicators.note: shortened, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Regret, briefly, over cutting a version of a text for study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' drops the last letter of the regret word, and 'cutting' means the shortened piece cuts into the printed version of the text.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep scholarship, the knowledge gained by study and learning.

clue.text: Season with leader absent for Italian team

indicators.note: the first letter, the leader, is missing

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: An Italian side plays a season without its captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with leader absent' drops the first letter of WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter Milan is a famous Italian football club, usually just called by its short name.

clue.text: Pay tribute to unionist over time in Manchester area

indicators.note: the two letters go in, inside the other word

parts.note: Sale is a town in Greater Manchester
U is an abbreviation for Unionist, as in Ulster Unionist

explanation.surface: Honouring a trade unionist who has served long in the Manchester area.
explanation.walkthrough: SALE is a town in Greater Manchester, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute someone is to honour or pay tribute to them.

clue.text: Organisation with initially big base gets serious setback

parts.note: a body is an organisation, as in a governing body

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: base means low or mean

explanation.surface: A large-based organisation suffers a serious setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A body blow is literally a punch to the torso; figuratively it is a severe blow or setback.
